transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I came in because things at work have been feeling really off. I’m a buyer, so I’m always looking at numbers and orders and launches, and I know how it’s supposed to look, you know? But I keep feeling like people there—and even some of the vendors—are tracking what I’m buying and messing with the launch numbers so I look stupid.

My supervisor keeps showing me reports and saying it doesn’t prove that, but I still can’t shake it. It’s like… I’ll try to focus on regular stuff, like what’s coming in for the next display, and then I’m back thinking about who changed what and why they’re watching my buys. That’s really what made me come in.
Can you tell me more about how you know people are watching or changing your work? Do you feel they are doing this specifically to target you or is it part of a larger plan?

I mean… I don’t have, like, a video of them doing it or anything. It’s more the pattern. I put in buys, then the launch numbers look wrong, or the timing looks off, and it feels too specific to just be an accident.

And yeah, it feels like it’s aimed at me, like they want me to look stupid or like I don’t know my job. My supervisor keeps showing me reports and saying, “See, this doesn’t show anyone changed anything,” but I still don’t buy it. Reports can be cleaned up. Vendors send weird little updates too, and then I start thinking about how they know what I’m ordering.

Sorry, I know I’m kind of jumping around. It’s just hard because I’ll be trying to look at the next display or normal inventory stuff, and my brain keeps going back to, “Who’s tracking this, who’s changing the numbers, and why me?”
Have you ever seen, heard, or sensed something that others around you don’t seem to notice?

Yeah… sometimes. Not like seeing things, really, but hearing. Like if I’m in the stockroom, or driving back after meeting a vendor, I’ll hear this man’s voice like it’s right behind me. It’ll say stuff like, “Move faster, Scott,” or it’ll laugh at what I picked.

And I’ll turn around, or look in the mirror if I’m driving, and there’s nobody there. It’s weird because the stockroom already has all these noises—carts, boxes, the lights buzzing—so I try to tell myself it’s that, but it sounds… too clear sometimes.
Outside of these experiences at work and hearing the voice, have you ever had other times where you felt like something was very real to you but others didn’t seem to notice it?

I guess… it mostly comes back to the work stuff. Like, I’ll try to tell myself maybe it’s just a mistake in the system or I’m overthinking the vendor updates, but it feels real. Really real.

Like people are watching what I’m buying, tracking the buys, and then the launch numbers get messed with so I look like I don’t know what I’m doing. My supervisor keeps showing me these reports, and he’s like, “There’s nothing here,” but reports don’t really prove nobody touched anything, you know?

Sorry, I know you asked outside of work… I just keep ending up there because that’s the thing I can’t shake.
Have you ever had any beliefs or ideas that others might find strange or unusual, even if they seemed completely true to you?

Yeah… probably the work thing. I know it probably sounds strange when I say it out loud, but it feels true to me. Like people at work, and even some of the vendors, are watching what I buy and then messing with the launch numbers so I look stupid.

And my supervisor keeps showing me reports like, “See, nothing happened,” but I don’t know… reports can be wrong, or cleaned up, or not show the real thing. That’s kind of what made me come in, honestly. I can’t shake it.

Sorry, I know I keep circling back to the same thing. It’s just when I’m looking at orders or displays or whatever, even normal stuff like endcaps and inventory, my head goes right back to that.
Have you ever had any beliefs or thoughts outside of work that you know might sound strange to others, but feel completely true to you?

Outside of work… I don’t know. Nothing really comes to mind like that.

I mean, sometimes I’ll be watching TV or scrolling on my phone and I’ll think, “That’s weird timing,” like an ad pops up right after I talked about something, but everybody says that happens now, so I don’t know if that counts. My cousin is always going on about phones listening, and then we get into this whole thing about apps and privacy policies, and I don’t even read those because they’re like ten pages long…

But, yeah, if you mean something like a strong belief that other people would think is really strange, outside of work, I’m not sure I have one. It’s mostly the work stuff that feels hard to ignore.
Have you ever had any unusual beliefs or thoughts outside of work that you know might sound strange to others, but feel completely true to you?

Outside of work, not really… I keep trying to think of something else, but it’s mostly that same thing.

What made me come in is I can’t shake this feeling that people at work—and maybe even some of the vendors—are tracking what I buy and then messing with the launch numbers so I look stupid. Like my supervisor shows me reports and says it doesn’t prove anything happened, but to me that doesn’t really settle it. Reports can miss things, you know?

So, outside of work, I don’t think I have something like that. It just keeps coming back to the buys and the numbers.
Have you ever had any experiences outside of work where you believed something strongly that others might not agree with or find hard to believe, even if it seemed completely true to you?

Outside of work, I’m still not really thinking of anything separate. I mean, I get suspicious about stuff sometimes, but the thing that feels real-real is work.

Like, what really made me come here is I can’t shake this feeling that people at work—and even some vendors—are tracking what I buy and then messing with the launch numbers so I look stupid. And my supervisor keeps showing me reports like they prove nothing happened, but I don’t know… reports don’t prove everything. They can leave things out. So even when people don’t agree with me, it still feels like that’s what’s happening.
Have you ever had any beliefs or suspicions outside of work that you strongly felt were true, even if others might not believe them or think they make sense?

I mean… outside of work, I don’t think there’s a separate thing like that. It all kind of circles back to work, honestly.

What really got me coming in here is I can’t shake this feeling that people at work—and maybe even some of the vendors—are tracking what I buy. Like they know what buys I’m making, and then the launch numbers come out wrong or get messed with so I look stupid. My supervisor keeps showing me reports like, “See, this doesn’t prove that,” but reports aren’t everything, you know? Numbers can be made to look clean.

So… not really outside of work, I guess. It’s mostly that.
Have you ever had any strong beliefs or experiences in your personal life that other people might find hard to believe, even if they seemed completely true to you?

In my personal life… I don’t know, I keep trying to separate it out, but it always comes back to work.

Like I’ll be at home making dinner or looking at my bank app, and then I start thinking about the buys I made and who saw them. It’s not like some random belief about my neighbors or anything. It’s more that I really feel like people at work—and maybe vendors too—are tracking what I buy and then messing with the launch numbers so I look stupid. My supervisor keeps showing me reports like that proves nothing happened, but I don’t know… reports can be cleaned up. Numbers can be made to say whatever. So even if other people think it sounds far-fetched, it feels true to me.
Have you ever had a strong belief that something was happening or was true, even when others told you it wasn’t, and this belief wasn’t related to your work or the launch numbers?

Not that I can really pin down, no. I mean, I get stuck on things sometimes, but if you’re saying totally not work, not the launch numbers… I don’t think so.

Like, I’ll overthink stuff at home too, but then it’s usually because I saw an email or I remembered a report, and then I’m checking my phone, and—sorry, that’s still work. So… no, I guess I haven’t had another separate belief like that.

Have you ever had a belief that something was happening or being done to you that others would say is not true, even if it seemed completely real to you, and this was not related to work or the launch numbers at all?

No, not really—not if it’s completely separate from work and the launch numbers.

I know I keep looping back to the same thing, but that’s honestly the thing that feels real to me. Like people at work, and maybe some of the vendors, are tracking what I’m buying, what buys I’m making, and then the numbers come out wrong so I look stupid. My supervisor shows me reports and says it doesn’t prove anything, but… I don’t know, reports can look clean and still not tell the whole story.

But outside of that? Like unrelated to all that? I can’t think of another one.
Have you ever believed something strongly—like something you could not let go of—that wasn’t related to work or the launch numbers, even when people gave you clear proof that it wasn’t true?

I mean… not really outside of that. The thing I can’t let go of is still the work thing.

Like, I know my supervisor keeps showing me reports and saying, “See, the numbers don’t prove anyone did anything,” but that doesn’t settle it for me. I keep thinking people at work—and maybe some vendors—are watching what I buy or tracking my buys somehow, and then the launch numbers get messed with so I look stupid.

And I know that probably sounds like I’m not answering your exact question, but that’s what made me come in. It’s not some other belief about, I don’t know, my apartment or strangers on the street. It’s that. I just can’t shake it.
